terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: Agent-estimated starting pose from solve_camera_pose.py (confidence 0.35, all orientation/position fields agentFill). Not yet confirmed by overlay review against the render -- that confirmation happens in Phase 5 render capture, per the tool doc: render the fitted mesh from this camera and adjust until silhouette/landmark alignment matches before trusting it.

objectClass.notes: Console-shaped hard-surface object. Bilateral silhouette: a low front control deck rising through a genuine curve (not a step) into a flat raised rear deck holding the cartridge bay. See Layer 1-3 of .img2threejs/analysis.md.

reasoning: Single swept-profile shell (front deck -> curve -> rear deck) is a moderate silhouette: one dominant curve, no organic surfacing, so silhouetteComplexity is mid-low.

Two macro components (shell, cartridge bay as its own macro since it is a genuine cut-in volume, not a decal) and four meso components (left front block, right front block, recessed eject column, raised rear deck) is a real but shallow hierarchy for a moderate tier.
Micro feature groups: the power/reset key pair, the eject pad, and the controller-port pair with pin rows -- three distinct groups, matching or exceeding the moderate floor of 2.
No repetition systems: nothing on this shell repeats at meaningful density (no vent grille exists on the real hardware per the primary reference, no fastener array).
Two material layers only: matte shell ABS and satin accent-key ABS. No metal, no glass, no fabric.
occlusionRisk is moderate because the rear face, underside and both flanks are unseen in every reference image; those regions are approximated from known bilateral symmetry, not measured.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate tier per COMPLEXITY_MINIMUMS: silhouette and hierarchy are real but shallow (one curve, four meso parts), no repetition system exists on the actual hardware, and two materials with local overrides (accent-key gloss, eject-pad wear) cover every visible surface distinction. needsMaterialLocalOverrides=true because the eject pad and eject column read as visually distinct sub-regions of the shell material, not full separate materials.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Two shallow parallel ridge/groove lines across the raised rear deck's top face, near its front edge.
Embossed pill-outline 'Nintendo' wordmark on the rear deck's top face, near its front-right corner.
Front-left relief block's outer corner shows a distinct stepped bevel edge where the block meets the lower shell.
POWER/RESET purple stadium-capsule keys, each with a bevel ring around the cap and embossed white text; EJECT sits between them as a darker grey recessed-looking pad, also with embossed text.
Controller port 1 shown in full: a rounded-rectangle recess with visible depth/shadow and a segmented pin-socket ridge inside.
Controller port 2's corner, partially visible -- confirms the same inset-recess construction as port 1.
EJECT pad reads as a distinctly darker grey than the surrounding shell -- confirmed by direct pixel sampling, not shading alone.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
mustNotDo: Do not add a vent grille or slot array to the top deck -- confirmed absent from the primary reference photo; a prior hand-built pass invented one and it was the most visible wrong feature on the model.
Do not mount the power/reset keys on the vertical front face -- both sit flat on the horizontal top face of the front deck.
Do not render the eject control as anything but the centre, grey control between the two purple keys -- left-to-right order is power, eject, reset.

Do not model the cartridge bay opening as a flat decal/plane painted on the surface -- it is a genuine recessed cut into the rear deck's top face and must read as a real cavity under the current lighting.
Do not guess unseen-geometry detail (rear face, underside, flanks) beyond the bilateral symmetry and flat-panel assumption already recorded in unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation.
Adjacent components must overlap by at least 0.02 world units at shared seams (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Raised or recessed relief and fasteners must be geometry, instanced micro-parts, or displacement; a map alone is an approximation (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

mustMatch: reference-derived PBR material response at or above 0.7 confidence when source pixels are usable
niceToHave: micro scratches, stains, chips, and dirt masks

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions.statement: Rear face, underside, and both flanks are unseen in every reference image; approximated as flat panels with bilateral symmetry, matching the SNES's published design.
The front-to-rear deck curve is interpolated from a single 3/4-angle view, not measured from an orthographic side profile; treated as an approximation.

Wordmark geometry (SUPER NINTENDO ENTERTAINMENT SYSTEM text, Nintendo logo) is below the resolution needed to trace as relief geometry; represented as a material-level local override (embossed emboss look), not modelled as separate geometry.

coordinateFrame.front: camera-facing side in the reference image
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: unit scale; adjust after first browser render

silhouette.boundingShape: a squat rectangular prism with a stepped-then-curved top profile: low flat front deck, a genuine curve (not a step) rising into a flat raised rear deck
silhouette.symmetry: bilateral about the depth axis (front-to-back centerline)
dominantCurves: a single continuous rise from the front control deck (40mm) to the rear deck (68mm), spanning roughly 48-142mm back from the front face -- not a step, a real curve
negativeSpaces: the recessed centre column between the two front relief blocks, carrying the EJECT control
landmarks: SUPER NINTENDO ENTERTAINMENT SYSTEM wordmark (rear deck front face)

observations: Bilateral shell, single swept profile: low front deck -> genuine curve -> raised rear deck holding the cartridge bay.
Front deck carries two raised relief blocks (left holds POWER + a controller port, right holds RESET + a controller port), separated by a flush recessed column carrying EJECT.
POWER and RESET are purple stadium-capsule keys mounted flat on the TOP face of their blocks, each with a bevelled cap edge and embossed white text.
EJECT is a grey pad, visually darker than the shell, set in the flush column between the two blocks, with embossed text.
Cartridge bay is a real recessed opening cut into the rear deck's top face, not a decal -- confirmed by visible depth/shadow at its edge.
Two shallow parallel styling ridge lines run across the rear deck's top face near its front edge.
Embossed pill-outline Nintendo wordmark sits on the rear deck's top face, near the front-right corner.
Shell material reads as matte/satin dielectric plastic: no metallic reflections, no anisotropic brushing, low saturation, roughness in the 0.6-0.7 range under diffuse studio light.
Controller ports are genuine inset rounded-rect recesses (visible depth at the opening edge) with a segmented pin-socket ridge visible inside, not flat dark decals.

componentTree.name: SNES console shell (swept profile)
componentTree.topologyRationale: A single moulded ABS shell: hard-edged panels with a genuine curved transition between deck heights, not an organic/continuous sculpt -- confirmed a curve, not a step, in the primary reference.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: extruded side profile (depth x height) swept across the shell's width -- the exact construction the local spec search confirmed (ExtrudeGeometry + bevel) for a moulded plastic shell

componentTree.name: Cartridge bay insert (rear deck top)
componentTree.topologyRationale: A distinct moulded insert framing the cartridge opening -- a real raised/recessed volume the reference shows depth and shadow at its edge for, not a flat decal painted on the deck.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: hard-surface moulded part with bevel-ready edges

componentTree.name: Front-left relief block
componentTree.topologyRationale: A raised volume standing proud of the front face with its own bevelled edge -- confirmed a real stepped edge, not a shaded flat panel, in the reference close-up (zone-r1c0).

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: hard-surface moulded part with bevel-ready edges

componentTree.name: Front-right relief block
componentTree.topologyRationale: Mirror of front-block-left across the shell's width centreline -- same bevelled proud edge.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: hard-surface moulded part with bevel-ready edges

componentTree.name: Eject column (flush centre strip)
componentTree.topologyRationale: The negative space between the two relief blocks: flush with the base shell front face (not proud like the blocks), carrying the EJECT pad -- a shallow surface region, not a standalone volume.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: hard-surface moulded part with bevel-ready edges

componentTree.name: POWER key (purple stadium cap)
componentTree.topologyRationale: A discrete moulded stadium-capsule cap sitting proud of the block's top face, approximated as a heavily bevelled box -- a true capsule primitive would round the wrong axis (a full 3D capsule, not a flat stadium key).

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: flat stadium cap: heavy bevel approximates the rounded-capsule silhouette seen in the reference close-up

componentTree.topologyRationale: Same construction as power-key -- confirmed identical stadium-cap shape and colour in the reference close-up (zone-r1c1), differing only in embossed text and position.

componentTree.name: EJECT pad (grey, flush centre column)
componentTree.topologyRationale: A shallow, distinctly darker-grey pad set into the flush eject column -- a colour/material distinction confirmed by direct pixel sampling (crops/eject-pad.png), not a modelled cavity.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: hard-surface moulded part with bevel-ready edges

componentTree.name: Controller port 1 (opening)
componentTree.topologyRationale: A genuine inset rounded-rect opening with visible depth and a segmented pin-socket ridge inside, confirmed in the reference close-up (zone-r2c1) -- not a flat dark decal.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: hard-surface moulded part with bevel-ready edges

reviewHistory.summary: Blockout (2 macro components: console-shell + cartridge-bay-insert) renders the correct macro silhouette -- real front-deck/curve/rear-deck profile from Nintendo's published dimensions, real sampled shell/accent colours. Camera hand-tuned against Tier 1 gate feedback: aspect-ratio delta 0.022 and scale delta 0.022 both comfortably pass (thresholds 0.05/0.08). Silhouette IoU stalls at 0.594 against the 0.85 threshold. Diagnosed the residual gap with a mask-diff visualization: the reference photo's own foreground mask is corrupted by a real specular highlight on the console's glossy top surface (sampled pixels ~241,243,244 vs background ~240s -- indistinguishable to simple background-difference thresholding), which the admission/masking pipeline cannot separate from true background. turntable_gate also flags small (1-2%) interior holes at 180/270 degrees, traced to the same class of near-white pixel confusion from a texture UV-streaking artifact on the procedural shell material, not a geometric defect (diagnose_render_multi_angle confirms zero degenerate views -- the form holds as a real volume from every angle).
matched: aspect ratio and scale of the overall silhouette (both pass their gates)
cartridge bay as a real raised/recessed macro volume, not a decal
mismatches: silhouette IoU below threshold, attributable in part to reference-photo mask corruption from a specular highlight
shell material shows diagonal UV-stretch streaking, a material-pass concern
no meso/micro detail yet -- by design, blockout only includes macro components

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Reach accepted visual fidelity first, then optimize without removing reference-critical geometry or surface layers.

lightingFromPhoto.description: Soft, large-area key light from upper-left-front, diffuse studio softbox -- long soft shadow falls to the lower-right of the console in the primary reference.
Broad ambient fill from the white background/surface bounce, keeping shadow-side shell values well above black.
Neutral exposure, ACES filmic tone mapping, sRGB output -- matches a clean product-photography look with no blown highlights on the shell.
Soft contact shadow directly under the shell where it meets the surface, consistent with the large soft key light.

Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.
